Lesley Ponraj, Appaswamy Thirumal Prabhakar, Shaik Atif Iqbal ahamed

Christian Medical College, Vellore, Tamil Nadu, India

Background and Aim: Visual processing impairment is a phenomenon described in parkinsonian disorders (PD). Tests used in this study are dot motion test (DMT), biological motion test (BMT), and noise pareidolia test (NPT). It still remains unknown whether these tests can predict cognitive impairment and whether it will be different in various parkinson’s disease subtypes. Our aim was to see if abnormalities in the higher-order visual impairment tests predicted severity, cognitive impairment, psychosis, and subtype of parkinsonism.

Methodology: This was a retrospective electronic medical record-based study done in 109 parkinsonian patients who underwent higher-order visual testing in a tertiary hospital.

Results: Performance on NPT was associated with vascular PD (F = 6.128, P = 0.015). Impairment in BMT was associated with the Hoehn & Yahr (HNY) stage (F = 10.049, P = 0.002). Poor performances on DMT (F = 7.221, P = 0.008) and BMT (F = 26.541, P < 0.001) were associated with low Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores predicting cognitive impairment. However, receiver operating characteristic curves of the tests did not show any significant results to predict the subtype of PD.

Conclusions: Higher-order visual testing, namely BMT and DMT, can predict the severity and cognitive impairment in patients with PD. NPT can be a tool to identify vascular contributions to PD.

Gaurav Chaudhary, Pawan T. Ojha, Akash Chheda, Kamlesh A. Jagiasi, Rakesh Singh, Arjun G. Shah, Anuradha P. Mahto, Aamna Maniyar, Shashank Nagendra, Billia K Appu, Karthik Gaud, Harshil Bagadia

Grant Medical College and JJ Hospital, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India

Background and Aim: Linezolid is used for treatment of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR TB). One of the common adverse effects associated with the treatment is peripheral neuropathy. Dose modification or interruption at the onset of peripheral neuropathy can prevent the development of irreversible deficits. We aim to study the clinical features, grade the severity of linezolid-induced peripheral neuropathy, and determine the effects of dose modification to avoid long-term deficits.

Methodology: MDR TB patients on linezolid treatment who developed peripheral neuropathy were studied. National Cancer Institute Neurosensory Scale was used to grade patients into mild, moderate, and severe neuropathy. Patients with mild neuropathy were continued on linezolid 600 mg. In patients with moderate neuropathy, the dose was reduced to 300 mg, and linezolid was withdrawn for severe neuropathy patients. Follow-up was done regularly and dose modified accordingly. End result was analyzed at 18 months of tuberculosis treatment completion.

Results: Eighty-four patients were included in the study. On presentation, 31 (36.9%) patients had mild neuropathy, 33 (39.28%) had moderate neuropathy, and 20 (23.8%) had severe peripheral neuropathies. Linezolid was stopped early in 41.6% patients. Improvement or stabilization of symptoms from onset was observed in 67.7% of patients in mild, 60.6% of patients in moderate, and 55% of patients in severe group. Moreover, 16.6% patients had persistent severe deficits at 18 months.

Conclusions: This study highlights the importance of grading linezolid-induced peripheral neuropathy and the need to provide standard guidelines for dose modification to prevent irreversible severe deficits.

Sayooja Sachithanandan

Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology (SCTIMST), Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India

Background and Aim: Clock drawing test (CDT) and cube construction test (CCT) are simple-to-administer tasks which require multiple cognitive domains. This study was aimed to find out the utility of these tests in relation to global tools for screening early cognitive impairment (ECI).

Methodology: All subjects meeting the inclusion and exclusion criteria were categorized into cognitively normal (CN), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and early dementia (ED) using standard clinical criteria. The mean CDT and CCT scores as well as types of qualitative errors were compared among the three groups. Spearman’s rank correlation test was used to study the relationship of various factors with CDT and CCT, and receiver operating characteristic curve was plotted to determine the utility of these tests as a screening tool in diagnosing MCI and ED from CN.

Results: A total of 228 subjects with a mean age of 69 ± 6.7 years were categorized into three groups. A cut-off score of 14 for CDT and 25 for CCT had optimal sensitivity and specificity to diagnose MCI from CN. Similar cut-off scores were obtained to diagnose ED from CN (12 for CDT and 22 for CCT). Age was negatively correlated and level of education was positively correlated to CDT and CCT score among CN subjects, but not in ECI subjects. Qualitative errors patterns of CDT were distinct among MCI and ED.

Conclusions: CDT and CCT were found to be performing better in diagnosing ED from CN than MCI from CN. CDT scored better as a screening tool than CCT possibly due to better objectivity in the scoring system.

Lakshmi Priya, Ashalatha Radhakrishnan, Ramshekhar N. Menon

Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology (SCTIMST), Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India

Background and Aim: Psychogenic nonepileptic events (PNEE) is one of the common disorders that feigns a true epilepsy or movement disorder, yet there are no current treatment guidelines to manage it even after setting up the diagnosis. This study aimed to determine the effect of viewing one’s own event as a novel treatment strategy in PNEE.

Methodology: This was a single-center, double-blinded, randomized controlled trial, where patients with at least one habitual psychogenic event recorded in the epilepsy monitoring unit were recruited. The participants were randomized (1:1) into two arms and all were given standard psychotherapy, while the intervention arm patients were shown their own recorded event in addition. The psychologic status (primary outcome), measured using standard questionnaires Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) and Quality of Life In Epilepsy-31 (QoLIE- 31) and event frequency (secondary outcome), was compared between baseline and follow-up at 3 months. Wilcoxon singed-rank test and Chi-square test were used to compare both the arms. Trial Registration information: CTRI/2021/04/033220

Results: Sixty-five participants (31 in the intervention /34 in the non-intervention arm) with a mean age of 32.3 years in the intervention arm and 29.2 years in the non-intervention arm were recruited. QoLIE-31 scores in the intervention group showed significant improvement in seizure worry (52.5, 95% confidence interval [CI] [32.5–60.0] to 44.0, 95% CI [33.0–52.0], P = 0.011), overall quality of life (52.5, 95% CI [32.5–60.0] to 65.0, 95% CI [52.5–72.5], P = 0.001), and emotional well-being (60.0, 95% CI [52.0–64.0] to 52.0, 95% CI [48.0–56.0], P = 0.004) compared to the scores in the non-intervention group. HADS-A, HADS-D, and event frequency improved favourably in both the arms.

Conclusions: Event viewing improves psychologic status in PNEE, especially regarding seizure worry and emotional well-being, without adverse outcomes.

Background and Aim: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) may cause vision loss with severe morbidity, thus necessitating the need for noninvasive biomarkers, such as optical coherence tomography (OCT), for deciding management strategies. Our study aimed to determine the association of OCT–retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness with clinical, radiologic features, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) opening pressure, and visual impairment and its potential to predict improvement in disease status.

Methodology: Our study was a retrospective cohort study of 66 patients with IIH hospitalized between 2019 and 2024. Patients were classified based on the degree of vision impairment as normal, mild, and severe. Statistical analysis was performed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences version-25. P-values were significant at <0.05.

Results: In our study, 92% were females; the median age of patients was 31 years. The median follow-up was 7 months. Disease cohorts included those with normal vision (52.3%), those with mild impairment (34.4%), and those with severe impairment (14.3%). 1. Patients with severe vision impairment had higher CSF opening pressures compared to patients with normal vision (P =0.001*) and patients with mild vision impairment (P = 0.007*). 2. OCT–RNFL showed significant correlation with grades of papilledema and degree of vision impairment in the right eye in all quadrants with early atrophy changes in the temporal quadrant (P –=0.026*) and thickening more prominent in the inferior quadrant (P = 0.032*). Conclusions: The multi-quadrant RNFL values, along with optic nerve and sheath diameter values could help in better characterization of disease status and serve as a biomarker for prognostication.

All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhubaneswar (AIIMS, Bhubaneswar), Odisha, India

Background and Aim: Cerebral infarct due to intracranial vasculopathy is the most severe complication of tuberculous meningitis (TBM). Transcranial Doppler (TCD) allows early detection and monitoring of cerebral hemodynamics. The aims and objectives of the study were to 1) detect cerebral vasculopathy in adult TBM patients by using TCD, 2) correlate TCD (Lindgaard ratio) with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) parameters, 3) study prognosis of the disease by serial TCD monitoring (comparing Modified Rankin Scale (mRS) with Lindegaard ratio (LR)), and 4) correlate TCD with neuroimaging.

Methodology: Consecutive TBM patients admitted in the Department of Neurology were evaluated. Serial TCD was performed two times during hospital stay and thereafter at 1- and 3-month follow-up after obtaining written informed consent. TCD findings (LR) were evaluated and then correlated with various parameters (CSF cells and protein, mRS, neuroimaging) by using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences version 26.

Results: Out of 33 TBM patients (22 male) who underwent TCD imaging, 23 patients (69%) showed high Lindegaard ratio (>3) at admission. Fifteen out of 16 patients of stage 3 and eight out of 13 patients of stage 2 had LR >3. There was statistically significant correlation between CSF cells and protein with LR. Twenty-one patients (58%) showed good mRS (0–2) with appropriate treatment after 1 month. On comparing mRS with TCD parameters, we found there was positive correlation at different time periods (at admission, at 1 month, and at 3 months).

Conclusions: Serial TCD can be used as a reliable modality for early diagnosis of intracranial vasculopathy in tubercular meningitis patients.

Bharanidharan G, Ramshekhar N Menon, George C. Vilanilam, Mathew Abraham, Chandrasekara kesavadas, Bejoy Thomas, Ashalatha Radhakrishnan

Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology (SCTIMST), Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India

Background and Aim: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) accounts for about 50%–73% of cases being referred for epilepsy surgery. The objective is to find whether the classical semiology in TLE has a role in predicting the postoperative outcome in patients with refractory epilepsy.

Methodology: We included 684 patients who underwent a detailed clinical evaluation, neuropsychologic assessment, 1.5 T/3 T magnetic resonance imaging, and video electroencephalogram (VEEG) monitoring, followed by a standard anterior temporal lobectomy from 1995 to 2008. They were followed up at 3 months, 12 months, and yearly with electroencephalogram. The outcome was classified into good if they did not have either seizure or aura, irrespective of the drugs used, and bad even if a single seizure occurred postoperatively.

Results: Of the 684 patients, 93.7% had behavioral arrest; 88.6% had automatisms, 86.7% had amnesia for the events, 74.6% had auras, and 63.6% had antecedents. All the classical semiology features were present in 37.7% of the whole cohort. In addition, 47.8% of the study population had good outcome till the last follow-up. The mean follow-up period was 75.6 months with a maximum follow-up of 14 years. Cases with antecedents had lesser probability of seizures at the last follow-up (P = 0.009). Febrile seizures as a separate variable were found protective (P = 0.021), and encephalitis was a risk factor (P = 0.026). Behavioral arrest was associated with poor seizure outcome following surgery (P = 0.006). No significant association with outcome was found for the presence of auras, automatisms, or amnesia.

Conclusions: Antecedents, especially febrile seizures and behavioral arrest had a favorable and poor surgical outcome, respectively. The combinations of different semiological features had no correlation with surgical outcome.

Background and Aim: Epilepsy, as global health concern, disproportionately affects children in India. School-based data is crucial for identifying these children and fostering inclusive environments. However, limited awareness often hinders optimal care. This study evaluates a longitudinal school-based educational intervention program designed to enhance epilepsy detection and management within India’s national health program (Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram [RBSK]).

Methodology: Conducted in a district of India, the study assessed an epilepsy education program in 406 government schools, enrolling over 63,000 children and 4169 teachers. Intervention: This 180-min program, delivered in the local language, targeted diverse stakeholders: teachers, health-care providers, and parents. It included lectures, role-plays, and discussions on epilepsy knowledge, management, and stigma reduction. The study employed mixed methods. Quantitative assessment reviewed RBSK child health registers to identify children referred to and confirmed for epilepsy before and after the intervention. Qualitative assessment used focus group discussions to explore program effectiveness.

Results: This school-based educational intervention demonstrated effectiveness and reached a large proportion of stakeholders. Epilepsy screening coverage and detection in schoolchildren significantly increased (baseline: 40/100,000 [95% confidence interval {CI}: 24–55]; year 3: 74/100,000 [95% CI: 54–95]). Stakeholders displayed improved knowledge and attitudes toward epilepsy and valued the program as appropriate, acceptable, feasible, and effective in improving epilepsy care.

Conclusions: This school-based educational intervention significantly improved epilepsy screening and detection in children. Stakeholders across schools and health care reported increased knowledge and confidence in managing epilepsy. With its positive impact on identification and support, this scalable program offers a promising approach to improve the care of children with epilepsy within national health initiatives.

Deenanath Mangeshkar Hospital and Research Center, Pune, Maharashtra, India

Background and Aim: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is a multisystem, autosomal dominant neurocutaneous syndrome. Epilepsy occurs in 80%–90% of patients, and over 50% of patients suffer from drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). We aimed to determine the predictive factors in surgical outcomes of TSC patients.

Methodology: This retrospective observational study included 43 patients of TSC admitted to the Epilepsy Monitoring Unit between 2015 and 2023. Patients’ clinical details, developmental status, magnetic resonance imaging, and 1-year postsurgical outcome status were recorded.

Results: Median age at presentation, median seizure onset age, and median epilepsy duration at presentation were 4 years, 6 months, and 3.2 years, respectively. Seizure onset below 2 years of age predicted delayed development. Depending on predominant seizure type, out of 43 patients 24 had focal seizures, four had spasms, six had tonic, and four had drop attacks. Out of 39 patients, six had polymorphic seizures in the form of diffuse-onset ictal rhythm in addition to focal onset, 14 had diffuse onset, and 19 had focal-onset ictal rhythm. Twenty-three patients underwent surgery, of whom 20 had tuber resection and three had corpus callosotomy. Engel class Ia was seen in 56.5% (13/23) of patients. All the patients with Engel Ia outcome had unifocal ictal rhythm on electroencephalogram (EEG). Engle class II was seen in 13% of patients (3/23). Seven patients (30.4%) had Engle class III and IV outcome. Out of these seven patients, five had spasms and four patients had Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS). On EEG, three patients had multifocal and 4 had generalized interictal epileptiform discharge (IEDs), while six patients had diffuse-onset ictal rhythm.

Conclusions: Presence of spasms, LGS, multifocal and generalized IEDs, and diffuse-onset ictal rhythms was associated with a poor postoperative seizure outcome.

National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro-Sciences, Bengaluru (NIMHANS, Bengaluru), Karnataka, India

Background and Aim: Sexual dysfunction in men with epilepsy (MWE) significantly affects the quality of life, but remains understudied. This research explores the factors contributing to sexual dysfunction and psychiatric comorbidities in MWE to enhance personalized care.

Methodology: A prospective study was conducted with 226 married men (150 MWE, 76 controls) from a neurology hospital in southern India between December 2021 and December 2023. The MWE group included 79 on monotherapy and 71 on polytherapy. Inclusion criteria were married men aged 21–45 years with epilepsy and on treatment for at least a year. Controls were healthy married men in the same age range. Exclusions included conditions affecting sexual health, substance abuse, and psychiatric medication use. Demographic and clinical data were collected. Sexual dysfunction was assessed using the Arizona Sexual Experience Scale (ASEX) and the Premature Ejaculation Diagnostic Tool (PEDT). Psychiatric symptoms were evaluated using the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale -21 (DASS-21) questionnaire. Data was statistically analyzed.

Results: Demographic characteristics were similar across groups. The polytherapy group had a significantly lower median age of epilepsy onset, longer epilepsy treatment duration, and higher seizure frequency. Significant sexual dysfunction (ASEX >18) was found in 19% of MWE, with 22.6% having definite premature ejaculation (PEDT >10). Diminished sexual drive was the most common (26%). Polytherapy had the highest ASEX scores, correlating with epilepsy, treatment duration, and seizure frequency. Psychiatric symptoms were highest in the polytherapy group. Valproate use significantly predicted sexual dysfunction (P = 0.007).

Conclusions: This large-scale study in India provides insights into the interplay between epilepsy, antiseizure medications, psychiatric comorbidities, and sexual dysfunction in men, informing improved holistic care.

Madhugandha Wahane, Ajay Goenka Goenka

Mahatma Gandhi Medical college, Rajasthan, Jaipur

Background and Aim: Seizure burden in neonates can be very high, majority of which do not have any clinical correlate. Its accurate diagnosis requires continuous video electroencephalogram monitoring (CVEM). The primary objective of this study was to precisely diagnose the frequency of electroclinical and electrographic seizures in a neonatal intensive care unit. The secondary objective was to assess the real-world implications in terms of the duration of hospital stay.

Methodology: A prospective analysis of CVEM in 140 patients between the ages of day 1 and day 60 of life was performed at a community hospital in India. The patients were divided into Group A patients with paroxysmal episodes and treated as electroclinical seizures, Group B patients with high risk of electrographic seizures but no electroclinical seizures, and a control group of 140 patients with similar clinical presentation before initiation of CVEM.

Results: CVEM was performed in 40 patients of Group A and 100 patients of Group B. The median monitoring duration was 18 h. A total of 652 seizures were captured, of which only 80 (12.2%) had clinical events. Among the 40 patients with paroxysmal events, 50% were confirmed to be electroclinical seizures. CVEM assisted in the medical management of 43% of infants. In the high-risk group (n = 100), electrographic seizures were recorded in 35% of patients. Twelve of these 35 (34%) patients were found to be in status epilepticus. The duration of hospital stay decreased from 15.4 to 11.5 days (P = 0.125) and from 18.3 to 14.1 days (P < 0.001) in Group A and Group B, respectively, compared to the control group.

Conclusions: The study highlights CVEM’s crucial role in promptly identifying and treating neonatal seizures, while also significantly reducing hospital stays, making CVEM a cost-effective tool.

Background and Aim: Autoimmunity and inflammation play important roles in the pathobiology of Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS). This study aimed to study the gene expression levels of the NLRP-3 inflammasome components in GBS and correlate them with the clinical and electrophysiologic profile.

Methodology: Fifty-one patients with “typical” GBS and 54 healthy controls were prospectively recruited from a single neurology unit after obtaining informed consent from May 2021 to March 2023. Results: The gene expression levels of Casp1 and Nlrp3 were significantly increased in GBS compared to controls (P = 0.006 and P = 0.035, respectively). No correlations were noted between the gene expression levels and the clinical severity or electrophysiologic subtypes.

Background and Aim: Sleep disturbances are commonly reported in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) with a prevalence of 40%–80% compared to typically developing children. Sleep, immune, and circadian dysfunction are interlinked and probably play a crucial role in ASD pathophysiology. Our aim was to correlate the impact of gene expression changes in inflammatory, circadian, and sleep homeostatic pathway-related genes on sleep dysfunction in ASD children and healthy controls (HCs).

Methodology: A prospective case–control study was conducted in departments of neurology, child and adolescent psychiatry, and human genetics at National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro-Sciences, Bengaluru between June 2022 and May 2024 after obtaining ethical approval. Orexin also correlated with CLOCK (P = 0.006) and IL-6 (P < 0.001). No significant differences were found for CLOCK, Orexin, IL-6, and STAT3 gene expressions; in addition, no correlations between gene expressions and sleep dysfunction were found in either group.

Conclusions:
BMAL1 gene has a significant role in ASD’s molecular mechanisms; its correlation with other genes implies the potential therapeutic targets for sleep disturbances in ASD.

Dulari Gupta, Shankar Prasad Gorthi, Sreehari Nil Dinesh, Sumit Nil Kharat, Chetna Nil Patil, Priscilla Nil Joshi, Vivek Nil Murumkar, Dhiraj Nil Dhane, Aditya Nil Ghadge, Soham Nil Sant

Bharati Vidyapeeth Medical College, Pune, Maharashtra, India

Background and Aim: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the world. Many outcome prediction scales have been devised, but are not frequently used in clinical practice. This study aims to harness the power of artificial intelligence (AI) in prediction of stroke outcomes at 3 months using stroke volume and clinical features.

Methodology: A single-center observational analytical study from a medical college in western India was conducted from Oct 2022 to May 2024. Data sets of patients with anterior circulation AIS were collected, including demographic data, risk factors, laboratory parameters, treatment, and outcomes at 3 months by modified Rankin Scale (mRS; dichotomized into good outcomes mRS <2 and bad outcomes mRS >3). Stroke volume was calculated using semi-automated segmentation on 3-D Slicer. Deep neural network was used for supervised model building.

Results: A total of 179 patients were studied, of whom 118 (65.9%) were male; their mean age was 59.36 ± 14.51 (range 25–92) years. Mean stroke volume was 24.64 ± 38 ml (range 0.05–249.6 ml). Of the patients, 118 (65.9%) had mRS at 3 months with good outcomes (mRS <2) and 61 (34.1%) had poor outcomes (mRS >3). Random forest model emerged as the best overall performer with high accuracy (0.89), sensitivity (0.96), and Jaccard Index (0.85), complemented by a robust receiver operating characteristic area under the curve of 0.93.

Conclusions: We have developed an AI stroke prediction model which can predict outcomes of stroke at 3 months with an accuracy of 89%. Such AI-based prognostication models can assist clinicians in counselling patients and relatives about the prognosis and functional outcomes after AIS.

Pradeep Kumar, Manabesh Nath, Annu Gulia, Manabesh Nath

All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi (AIIMS, New Delhi), India

Background and Aim: Acute ischemic stroke is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Various endovascular and thrombolytic interventions are employed to achieve successful recanalization, yet their comparative efficacy remains unclear. This study aims to comprehensively compare these treatments through a network meta-analysis.

Methodology: We conducted a network meta-analysis of published studies encompassing a broad range of interventions, including Solitaire, TREVO, MERCI, Penumbra, intravenous thrombolysis (IVT), intra-arterial thrombolysis (IAT), standard treatment (ST), Mix-Mechanical Thrombectomy (MT)-Devices, MT + IVT, and MT + IAT. Risk ratio (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) was calculated to assess the efficacy of each treatment in achieving successful recanalization (thrombolysis in cerebral infarction (TICI) or thrombolysis in myocardial infarction (TIMI) flow)

Results: A total of 184 studies (40 randomized controlled trials and 144 cohorts) were included in our network meta-analysis. Comparison between MERCI and TREVO demonstrated a significantly higher risk associated with MERCI devices (RR = 2.42; 95% CI 1.15–5.09). Conversely, comparing Penumbra versus MERCI indicated a considerably lower risk with Penumbra (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.52–0.92). In addition, MT + IVT was found to have a significantly lower risk compared to Mix-MT-Devices (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.40–0.77). ST versus MT + IVT highlighted a significantly higher risk with ST (RR 5.94, 95% CI 2.64–13.30). TREVO versus Solitaire and IVT versus Penumbra showed no significant differences. The network plot suggests that Mix-MT-Devices, MT + IVT, and MT + IAT emerged as pivotal interventions, supported by substantial comparative data.

Conclusions: Future studies should focus on filling these gaps to optimize treatment strategies and improve patient outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.

ABVIMS and Dr RML Hospital, New Delhi, India

Background and Aim: Studies on non-invasive brain stimulation techniques such as transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) have shown positive results in rehabilitating chronic aphasia patients after a stroke. However, their effects on acute ischemic stroke patients with aphasia have not been well studied.

Methodology: This was a prospective, double-blinded, randomized trial. Using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, 28 patients were enrolled and randomized into two 14-patient groups. One group received 5 days of anodal tDCS to the Broca’s area, whereas the other received sham stimulation. The outcomes were a change in the accuracy, reaction time, and picture naming test (PNT) scores on the Indian Council of Medical Research PNT at 4 weeks after the last session of anodal tDCS.

Results: Both groups had similar baseline characteristics. Naming Accuracy results at 4 weeks after tDCS compared to baseline were statistically significant in the anodal tDCS group (Friedman test, P = 0.002). Reaction Time results at 4 weeks after tDCS compared to baseline were statistically significant in the anodal tDCS group (Friedman test, P = 0.001). PNT score results at 4 weeks after tDCS compared to baseline were statistically significant in the anodal tDCS group (Friedman test, P = 0.002). No such results were obtained in the sham stimulation group (P = 0.992). A mixed analysis of variance comparing the anodal tDCS and sham stimulation groups showed a significant effect of both time and stimulation on both groups, eliminating time as a confounding factor (F (4, 104) = 4.27, P = 0.003 for Accuracy, F (4, 104) = 4.47869, P = 0.004 for Reaction Time, and F (4, 104) = 4.42, P = .002 for PNT scores).

Conclusions: tDCS is helpful in patients with aphasia after acute stroke, but larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

Background and Aim: Stroke is the fourth leading cause of death and fifth leading cause of disability in India. Our aim was to assess predictors of good functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0–2) at 3 months and early neurologic improvement (ENI) - National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) reduction by 8 or NIHSS of 0/1 at 24 h in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients.

Methodology: A single-center prospective cohort study recruiting 311 adult AIS patients with pre-stroke mRS 1, within 72 h of ictus, fulfilling the inclusion and exclusion criteria was conducted from February 2022 till November 2023.

Results: Of the patients, 66% were males, having a mean age of 56 years (±16.18); 53% were hypertensive, 35% were diabetic, 33% had dyslipidemia, 38% consumed tobacco, and 23% consumed alcohol. Results also showed that 22%, 31%, 27%, 5%, and 14% had small vessel disease (SVD), large artery atherosclerosis, cardioembolic stroke, stroke of other determined etiology, and stroke of undetermined etiology, respectively. Mean systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), NIHSS at presentation, Computed tomography - Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (CT-ASPECTS), collateral score, time to hospital arrival, time to thrombolysis, and time to thrombectomy were 147 mmHg (±28.58), 86 mmHg (±16.4), 6 (±1), 11 (6–17), 6 (±3), 3 (±1), 6.5 h (3.5–12.5), 5.5 h (3.5–9), and 3.5 h (2.5–4.5), respectively. In addition, 52% had large vessel occlusion (LVO) and 38% achieved ENI. On univariate analysis, younger age of ictus, lower NIHSS at 0, 24, and 72 h, higher GCS at presentation, higher CT-ASPECTS, absence of LVO, higher multiphase computed tomography angiography (mTCA) collateral score, Trial of ORG 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment (TOAST) of SVD, ENI, absence of cardiac chamber enlargement on echocardiography, absence of arrhythmia diagnosed by either echocardiogram/electrocardiogram/Holter, intake of dual antiplatelet, those who did not undergo decompression surgery, higher serum albumin, lower C-reactive protein, lower D-dimer, lesser time from ictus to hospital, and reduced duration of hospital stay, all were prognostic factors for good outcome at 3 months. On performing multivariate regression, NIHSS at presentation, age, achieving ENI, intake of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), and absence of arrythmia were significant independent predictors of good outcome at 3 months after adjusting for confounding factors. With the increase in age and NIHSS at 0 h, chances of good outcome significantly decreased with adjusted odds ratio of 0.943 (0.889–0.999, P = 0.049) and 0.791 (0.656–0.954, P = 0.014), respectively. Achieving ENI, usage of DAPT, and absence of arrythmia had higher odds of achieving good outcome with odds ratio (OR) of 68.688 (28.127–167.742), 0.268 (0.096–0.749), and 0.296 (0.091–0.962), respectively. On performing multivariate regression, lower admission NIHSS, intravenous thrombolysis (IVT), use of DAPT, absence of arrythmia, and right hemispheric stroke were independent predictors of ENI. With the increase in NIHSS at 0 h, chances of ENI significantly decreased with adjusted odds ratio of 0.795 (0.717–0.881, P < 0.0001). With IVT, use of DAPT, absence of arrythmia, and right hemispheric stroke, odds of ENI increased with OR of 4.312 (2.258–8.233), 0.077 (0.015–0.395), 0.226 (0.112–0.456), and 0.153 (0.058–0.406), respectively.

Conclusions: Improving our knowledge about predictive factors might enhance rehabilitative procedures in AIS patients.

Amrita School of Medicine, Kochi, Kerala, India

Background and Aim: Post-transplant stroke incidence usually ranges from 1.1% to 8% in kidney transplant recipients and from 1.8% to 4% in liver transplant recipients. Our aim was to assess the clinical features and 3-month outcome of stroke after solid organ transplant in a study of 35 cases from a comprehensive stroke center. We tried to investigate the etiologies and characteristics of stroke occurring after transplantation.

Methodology: We conducted a retrospective analysis of patients who underwent solid organ transplantation (liver, kidney with pancreas) at Amrita Hospital from 2009 to 2023. Patient demographics, comorbidities, National institutes of health stroke scale (NIHSS), modified Rankin Scale, type of stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic), TOAST classification of ischemic stroke, immunotherapy, and stroke treatment were recorded. Data were retrieved from electronic medical records.

Results: Out of 2050 patients, 35 experienced a stroke, post-transplantation: 17 were liver transplant recipients and 18 were kidney transplant recipients. Among these 35 patients, 17 had ischemic strokes, 16 had hemorrhagic strokes, and two had transient ischemic attacks. The mortality rate was 1.02% in liver transplant group (six patients succumbed) and 1.8% in kidney transplant group (10 patients succumbed). Unfortunately, 16 of the 35 patients succumbed to their conditions, with hemorrhagic stroke (10 patients) being the most common cause of death, regardless of their comorbidities.

Conclusions: Our study underscores the critical need for vigilant monitoring and management of stroke risk factors in post-transplant patients, particularly within a few months of perioperative period for liver transplant recipients and throughout life for kidney transplant recipients.

Shriram Chandra Bhanja Medical College and Hospital Cuttack, Odisha, India

Background and Aim: Movement disorders (MDs) are characterized by impaired voluntary movement, the presence of involuntary movements, or both. Children more commonly demonstrate hyperkinetic MDs, such as tics, chorea, ballismus, dystonia, myoclonus, stereotypies, and tremor, than hypokinetic disorder. Determining their etiology is important for specific treatment and prognostication. This study aimed to find out the clinical pattern of various MDs in children and to establish their etiology and outcome.

Methodology: A prospective observational study was conducted from September 2022 to October 2023 in a tertiary care hospital in eastern India. Children from 6 months to 15 years of age presenting with involuntary movements to the outpatient department and wards of neurology and pediatrics were included. History and clinical examination were carried out with a predesigned proforma. A diagnostic workup was done, and results were analyzed to find the pattern of MDs and their etiology. Patients were followed up over a period of 3 months for the outcome.

Results: Out of 84 patients, isolated MDs were seen in 58 (69%) and mixed MDs in 26 (31%). Among isolated MDs, dystonia (n = 32, 55%), tremor (n = 9, 15%), and chorea (n = 6, 10%) were common, whereas among mixed type MDs, majority were dystonia plus chorea (n = 18, 69%).

Conclusions: Etiologies of MDs specific to this part of India are infection-related, genetic/metabolic, and cerebral palsy. A significant number of children had more than one type of MD. Early recognition and specific diagnosis are required for better outcome.

Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology (SCTIMST), Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India

Background and Aim: We aimed to describe the clinical profile and evolution of adult patients with isolated focal and segmental dystonia presenting for treatment in our Botulinum toxin (BoNT) clinic, and the response to treatment, over 20 years.

Background and Aim: Young-onset Parkinson’s disease (YOPD) refers to patients who develop Parkinson’s disease earlier in life, significantly impacting social, occupational, and familial dynamics. Background and Aim: Non-parkinsonian tremors (NPTs) are a heterogeneous group of tremor disorders, with essential tremor (ET) being the most common type. Methodology: This cross-sectional study enrolled 202 patients aged more than or equal to 18 years with NPT attending the movement disorder clinic at a rural tertiary care hospital in Gujarat, India, over 14 months. Results: The prevalence of NPT was 2.34% in the neurology outpatient clinics and 28.25% in the movement disorder clinic. ET, ET-plus, and dystonic tremors had similar prevalence, each constituting nearly one-fifth of the study population. Significant differences were observed in age of onset, gender distribution, family history, and tremor severity among tremor subtypes.

Conclusions: This study provides a comprehensive assessment of NPT prevalence, clinical characteristics, and severity in a rural western Indian population using the 2017 MDS classification. SCTIMST, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India

Background and Aim: Focal epilepsies constitute about 50%–60% of all epilepsies and are regarded as acquired disorders with underlying structural etiology. Due to the general emphasis on developmental–epileptic encephalopathies, sparse data exists regarding the diagnostic yield of genetic testing in focal epilepsies. We aimed to study the genotype–phenotype correlates of monogenic focal epilepsies and their impact on the understanding of pathophysiologic mechanisms and outcome variables.

Methodology: We conducted a single-center retrospective study of prospectively maintained records with data of all monogenic epilepsies between 2019 and 2023. The probands fulfilling the criteria for focal epilepsy with underlying genetic etiology were included, and the electroclinical data was collected. Variant interpretation was stratified as per American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics(ACMG) guidelines. The probands were further divided based on underlying pathophysiologic mechanism into channelopathies and non-channelopathies, and the electroclinical and outcome data were compared between them. Predictors of seizure freedom were analyzed.

Results: Of the 620 probands who underwent genetic testing between 2019 and 2023, 142 patients were included. Variants involving ion channels 38 [34.9%], receptors (5 [4.6%]), transporters (3 [2.8%]), synaptopathies (5 [4.6%]), cell proliferation (3 [2.8%]), metabolic (10 [9.2%]), and other multiple function proteins (44 [41.3%]) were included. Comparison analysis between channelopathies and non-channelopathies showed predominant infantile-onset (P = 0.023), predominant focal seizures plus (added semiology) (P = 0.029), atypical febrile seizures (P = 0.028), nocturnal predominant seizures (P = 0.021), and poor seizure outcome (P = 0.037) in the latter. The factors associated with the absence of seizure freedom were the presence of myoclonic jerks in addition to focal semiology (P= 0.009), global developmental delay (P = 0.015), psychomotor regression (P = 0.044), presence of antecedent febrile seizures (P = 0.006), bihemispheric interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) (P = 0.045), absence of sleep structures (P = 0.045), and channelopathies (P = 0.037).

Conclusions: Identification of genetic focal epilepsy syndromes has significant implications in predicting surgical outcome, accurate prognostication, and potentially altering management strategies.

Background and Aim: Several neurologic diseases present with complex phenotypes caused by genetic mutations. These are labelled “neurogenetic syndromes” and are diagnosed by appropriate genetic testing. As these tests become increasingly accessible and affordable in our country, neurologists must be familiar with their benefits and limitations. We present here a retrospective, cross-sectional study examining the yield of whole exome sequencing (WES) in suspected neurogenetic diseases.

Methodology: We included 205 patients suspected of having neurogenetic diseases and visiting the neurology department of a tertiary care center between January 2018 and January 2024 for this study. Results: Ninety-one patients showed “pathogenic” mutations, giving a diagnostic yield of 44%. Seventy patients (34%) showed VUS and 44 (22%) patients did not show any mutation. Conclusions: This study should inform future clinical practice when it comes to diagnosis, prognosis, surveillance, family planning, disability rights, academic research, drug development, and treatment of neurology patients seen in clinical practice.

All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Rishikesh (AIIMS, Rishikesh), Uttarakhand, India

Background and Aim: In Guillain–Barré (GBS) patients with dysautonomia, the sympathovagal balance is shifted toward sympathetic overactivity (SO). This study assessed the role of prazosin (1-blocker) in the management of SO.

Methodology: This prospective cohort study was conducted during Jan 2022 and Sept 2023. Thirty-two GBS patients with dysautonomia received prazosin (2.5–10 mg three times a day) (prazosin arm). For comparison, we also included 33 age- and disability-matched GBS patients with dysautonomia (control group), who did not receive prazosin, from a prospectively maintained GBS registry and admitted during Feb 2018–Dec 2021. The primary outcome was fluctuations during the 24-h period in systolic blood pressure (SBP; maximum SBP – minimum SBP, in mmHg) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP; maximum DBP – minimum DBP) at 15 days. Secondary endpoints were days to resolution of dysautonomia, duration of hospital stay, in-hospital mortality, adverse events, and 3- month disability.

Results: The median age was 36 (interquartile range 25–49) years. The demographic and clinical parameters were comparable. The mean fluctuations in SBP (30 ± 15.8 vs. 44 ± 17.6 mmHg, P = 0.002) and DBP (21 ± 10.6 vs. 28 ± 9.3 mmHg, P = 0.02) at 15 days were significantly lower in the prazosin group. Prazosin resulted in significantly earlier normalization of dysautonomia compared to the control group (median 15 vs. 20 days, P = 0.01). However, duration of hospital stay (30 vs. 27 days, P = 0.54) and good recovery at 3 months (71.9% vs. 63.6%, P = 0.48) were comparable. Three (9.3%) patients in the prazosin group developed hypotension, while two patients in the no-prazosin group developed posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES).

Conclusions: Prazosin resulted in earlier normalization of dysautonomia and lower incidence of PRES, but did not affect 3-month outcome and duration of hospital stay.

Background and Aim: Thymectomy is an integral part of treatment strategies for both thymomatous and non-thymomatous myasthenia gravis (MG). Both subtypes differ in terms of their clinical profile, treatment response, and natural history. There is scarce literature regarding the long-term outcomes in thymomatous MG, especially with regards to the predictive role of thymus pathology and the timing of thymectomy.

Methodology: This was an observational study of MG patients admitted in a quaternary referral hospital, who underwent thymectomy and had at least 6 months follow-up. Clinical profile, thymus pathologies, and outcomes at the last follow-up were recorded.

Results: Eighty-two patients (42 females, 40 males) were included in the study. Their mean age was 43.58 years (standard deviation 12.76). Majority (95%) had generalized MG. Thymoma grades were B2 (33.7%), AB (26.5%), B1 (18.1%), and B3 (15.7%). Masaoka stages were stage 1 (33.7%), IIA (17.1%), IIB (30.5%), and III–IV (18.7%). Conclusions: Majority of the patients had good outcomes. Masaoka staging was significantly associated with overall survival. There was no significant association between tumour pathology and MG course. Coexistent thymic hyperplasia was associated with a higher chance of active MG at follow-up, which is attributable to changes in secondary lymphoid organs. Meticulous tumour surveillance is paramount for good long-term outcomes.

NRS Medical College & Hospital, Kolkata, India

Background and Aim: Idiopathic Parkinson’s disease (IPD) patients have progressively increased slowness, rest tremors, rigidity, and postural instability. Postural stability depends on sensory inputs from visual, auditory, and somatosensory modalities. We tried to find out important cut-off values of visual evoked potential (VEP), brainstem auditory evoked response (BAER), and short-latency somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEP) which determine the postural stability in IPD patients.

Methodology: Fifty IPD patients were recruited in a cross-sectional observational study. “Pull test” was used to determine postural stability. Patients were sub grouped into tremor dominant variant (TV; n = 37) and postural instability and gait disorder (PIGD; n = 13). We generated receiver operating characteristic curves to classify patients into posturally stable and unstable and measured VEP, BAER, and SSEP cut-off values. Area under the curve >0.8 was taken as significant.

Results: Significant VEP N75, P100, and N145 cut-off values were noted in IPD and its subgroups (TV and PIGD) bilaterally. Except for wave I, the latency of all other BAER waves showed significant cut-off values bilaterally in IPD and subgroups (TV and PIGD). Most BAER cut-off values in the IPD and TV subgroups reached 100% specificity. No significant SSEP values were noted.

Conclusions: We found many evoked potential significant cut-off values determining the postural stability in IPD and its subgroups (TV and PIGD). A lesser vestibular compensatory support in PIGD led them to a more severe phenotype than TV.

Milan Mori, Ashish Duggal, Jyoti Garg, B. K. Bajaj, Ashish Kumar Duggal

ABVIMS& Dr RML Hospital, New Delhi, India

Background and Aim: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is characterized by progressive loss of response to dopaminergic therapy, thereby posing a significant therapeutic challenge. Deep brain stimulation has proven efficacy, but carries risks and is not possible in all patients. Non-invasive brain stimulation like transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), which modulates cortical activity, has shown promising results and may provide an alternative therapeutic modality.

Methodology: This was a prospective, double-blinded, randomized trial. Thirty patients were enrolled and randomized to receive either true or sham stimulation. The true stimulation group received two or three sessions of bihemispheric anodal tDCS per week for a total of 10 sessions, whereas the other group received sham stimulation in the same settings. The primary outcome was to compare the changes in motor function and gait assessed by Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale (MDS UPDRS) Part-III and TUG (Timed up and Go) score, respectively, at 1 week after the repetitive stimulation compared to that of sham group of tDCS. A mixed-model analysis of variance was used to compare the UPDRS scores and TUG as dependent variables between the two groups and stimulation, time, and interaction between stimulation and time as fixed variables.

Results: Both groups had similar baseline characteristics. The study found no significant interaction between stimulation and time in TUG (F = 2.29, P = 0.11) and UPDRS Part III scores (F = 2.1, P = 0.12). However, subgroup analysis of bradykinesia scores in UPDRS III revealed a significant interaction between time and type of stimulation (F = 4.328, P = 0.018), indicating that tDCS may have a beneficial effect on bradykinesia.

Conclusions: tDCS of the motor and prefrontal cortices may have therapeutic potential in PD with some improvement in bradykinesia over time. However, optimized stimulation parameters and protocols need to be established to make the technique clinically viable with larger studies.

Background and Aim: Hemispherotomy is an effective surgical approach for drug-resistant epilepsy patients with hemispheric epileptogenic lesions. We aimed to determine the surgical outcome as well as its predictors in patients undergoing hemispherotomy for drug-resistant epilepsy and to compare the outcome between the pediatric age group and above.

Methodology: This is a single-center retrospective study. Using logistic regression, we evaluated the correlation between clinical, demographic, electroencephalography (EEG; ictal, interictal, and postoperative EEG), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain variables, and the postsurgical outcome. We grouped patients based on age, pathology, EEG findings and evaluated the outcome in terms of postoperative seizure outcome.

Results: One hundred and fifty patients’ mean age at surgery was 11.21 + 6.39 years, and their mean follow-up was 16.79 + 8.38 years. Eighty-nine patients (59.3%) were of age less than 12 years (pediatric group). Most common pathology was porencephalic cyst (33 patients, 30%), and MRI showed contralateral pathology in 15 patients (10%). EEG showed lateralized IEDs in 59 patients (39.3%) and ipsilateral ictal onset in 66 patients (44%). Moreover, 67.3% were seizure free and 82.7% had Engel class I outcome at the last follow-up with a mean follow-up of 5.65 years. At 5-year follow-up, the seizure outcome was better in the adolescent–adult age group (51.7% vs. 35.2%; P-value: 0.048).

Conclusions: Knowledge about independent determinants of surgical outcome following hemispherotomy is crucial for the counselling of patients and families.

Institute of Medical Sciences, Varanasi (IMS, Varanasi), Uttar Pradesh, India

Background and Aim: Post-stroke spasticity is a common complication of stroke. The study evaluated the efficacy of a posture opposite to the typical spastic posture, that is, Supinated forearm, Extended fingers and elbow, and Abducted and externally rotated shoulder (SEA), with the wrist in neutral position in acute stroke patients with flaccid weakness, in prevention of development of spasticity.

Methodology: Hemodynamically stable acute stroke patients between 18 and 80 years of age with flaccid upper limb weakness presenting within 72 h were included. This is a prospective, single-center, randomized, open-label trial with blinded endpoint assessment.

Results: Of 170 acute stroke patients, 76 met the inclusion criteria. Thirty-eight patients were randomized in each splint (Group 1) and control arm (Group 2). Ten patients were lost to follow-up. Of the remaining 66 patients (34 in splint and 32 in control), the median age of patients was 55 years. Forty-two (64%) patients were male. There was no significant difference in baseline demographic, clinical, radiologic, and biochemical parameters between the two groups. At 3 and 6 months, there was significant difference (P < 0.05) in modified Ashworth upper limb spasticity score at the elbow, forearm (pronation and supination), wrist, and fingers between the two groups. Barthel Index for Activities of Daily Living was also significantly better in group 1 at 3 and 6 months. However, there was no difference in modified Rankin Scale during follow-up.

Conclusions: SEA posture, if applied early in acute stroke patients, is effective in reducing the grade of upper limb spasticity.

National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro-Sciences, Bengaluru (NIMHANS, Bengaluru), Karnataka, India

Background and Aim: Mutations in the genes SLC52A2 and SLC52A3, which encode the riboflavin transporters RFVT2 and RFVT3, respectively, cause Brown–Vialetto–Van-Laere (BVVL) syndrome. Typically, patients present with sensorineural deafness and progressive pontobulbar palsy. Other features include sensorimotor axonal neuropathy, optic atrophy, and respiratory compromise. Here, we describe the clinical and genetic spectrum of eight genetically confirmed BVVL syndrome patients, which closely mimics the elusive Madras motor neuron disease (MMND).

Methodology: This was a retrospective observational study on eight patients with BVVL syndrome and corresponding genetic variants. Baseline demographic, clinical, and neurophysiology details were recorded, and genetic analysis was done by next generation sequencing.

Results: The mean age at disease onset was 11.25 (range: 7–16) years. All had varying illness durations, with a mean duration of 6.75 (range: 3–12) years. All had severe sensorineural hearing loss, dysarthria and severe hypophonia, tongue atrophy and fasciculations, impaired tandem gait, and sensory ataxia. Weakness and atrophy of limb muscles were noted in five, facial weakness in four, sensory symptoms in three, and cranial nerve palsy was observed in 9–11 patients (5). Of the eight patients, five novel variations (two homozygous and two heterozygous variants in the SLC52A3 gene and one heterozygous variant in the SLC52A2 gene) and previously reported one homozygous and one heterozygous variant in SLC52A3 were noted. Six of eight patients reported significant clinical improvement after 3–6 months of high-dose riboflavin therapy (600 mg/day).

Conclusions: This report highlights the importance of genetic confirmation of all patients suspected to have MMND/BVVL syndrome and not mislabel cases as MMND, for which still further advanced genetic testing is warranted.

Background and Aim: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is associated with high mortality and morbidity. Uncertainty still exists regarding benefit of surgery in the management of spontaneous supratentorial ICH (sICH), especially of the basal ganglia and thalamus. Studies have not shown clinical benefit of early surgical management compared to best medical management plus delayed surgery, when necessary. Our aim was to compare the efficacy of different neurosurgical interventions and best medical management with best medical management alone.

Methodology: We conducted a single-center, retrospective study in sICH patients at a tertiary care center in India between January 2015 and December 2022. Results: Among 2600 stroke patients screened, 661 had sICH. Median age was 55 years, and 250 patients (37.8%) underwent neurosurgical intervention. However, the ICH score at admission was lower in the conservatively managed group and after adjustment for ICH score, there was no statistically significant difference between the two. Among the interventions, patients undergoing decompression craniectomy had the best functional outcome.

Conclusions: Neurosurgical intervention was not associated with better functional outcome when compared to conservative management.

Background and Aim: This meta-analysis aims to systematically assess the safety and efficacy of stem cell therapy in patients with multiple sclerosis (MS).

Methodology: We conducted a comprehensive literature search across electronic databases, including PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. Inclusion criteria comprised randomized controlled trials reporting on the effect of stem cell therapy in MS patients. Background and Aim: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is an important differential of Parkinson’s disease. The 2017 PSP diagnostic criteria classify it into cortical and subcortical variants. Subcortical variants have longer disease duration and slower progression rate. However, progressive supranuclear palsy- Richardson syndrome (PSP-RS) is overrepresented compared to other variants. Midbrain to pons ratio in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) aids in PSP diagnosis and subclassification. We aimed to subclassify PSP into cortical and subcortical types and identify the clinical and radiologic correlation in PSP patients.

Methodology: This was a retrospective observational study performed in Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences, Faridabad. Patients who attended movement disorder clinic at Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences, Faridabad, between August 2022 and April 2024, and were provisionally diagnosed as PSP were included as the study population. Clinical and radiologic data were collected using MS Excel. Statistical analysis was then performed.

Results: Out of the total 105 patients, four patients could not be traced. Thirty-four out of 101 patients were females (67 males). The mean age at symptom onset was 66.9 years, and the mean disease duration at presentation was 3.8 years. Most common clinical subtype was progressive supranuclear palsy-corticobasal syndrome (PSP-CBS) (31), followed by progressive supranuclear palsy-parkinsonism (29), progressive supranuclear palsy- Richardson syndrome (21), progressive supranuclear palsy - frontotemporal dementia (PSP-FTD) (18), and progressive supranuclear palsy-progressive gait freezing (3). Most common presenting feature was akinetic rigid syndrome, followed by cognitive dysfunction, dystonia, and gait freezing. The midbrain to pons ratio was measured in 47 cases. Mean midbrain:pons ratio was 0.15 in PSP-RS subgroup, 0.245 in PSP-CBS, 0.22 in PSP-P, and 0.21 in PSP-FTD subgroup. PSP-CBS patients had asymmetric cortical atrophy.

Conclusions: PSP subtypes other than PSP-RS are underrepresented. Classifying PSP into cortical or subcortical subtypes based on clinical and radiologic assessment may aid treatment and prognostication.

Army Hospital Research & Referral, New Delhi, India

Background and Aim: Movement disorders are a prominent and common feature in many autoantibody-mediated neurologic diseases and present as varied clinical presentations. This is especially crucial as they are potentially curable and sometimes a harbinger of an underlying tumour. This study aims to describe the variability of presentations, etiology, management, follow-up, and outcome of autoimmune encephalitis (AIE), a potentially reversible cause of movement disorder.

Methodology: We evaluated eight patients who presented with movement disorders associated with AIE at our tertiary care center between 2021 and 2023. All patients were treated and followed up as per standard protocol.

Results: We evaluated eight patients who presented with movement disorders in association with AIE. Two patients received second-line therapy consisting of rituximab (Table 2). One patient with paraneoplastic opsoclonus myoclonus ataxia syndrome received adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and required surgical removal of the tumor. All patients are in remission; six patients are on maintenance immunosuppressants with azathioprine (n = 3), mycophenolate mofetil (n = 3), and two are on rituximab.

Conclusions: Our observations suggest that a high index of clinical suspicion with early and aggressive management of these disorders will increase the likelihood of better outcomes.

All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi (AIIMS, New Delhi), India

Background and Aim: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 12 (SCA12) is the most common autosomal dominant ataxia in northern India. In clinical practice, non-ataxia manifestations are frequently observed in SCA12 patients, which require early diagnosis and management to improve quality of life. Our aim was to study non-ataxia manifestations of SCA12, which are currently lacking in literature.

Methodology: We conducted a single-center, cross-sectional study on 60 genetically confirmed cases of SCA12. We analyzed non-ataxia manifestations by using the following validated scales: Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MOCA), Hamilton Depression Scale (HAM-D), Hamilton Anxiety Scale (HAM-A), Validated Sleep Questionnaire, and short form health survey questionnaire (SF-36), which were used to assess cognition, depression, anxiety, sleep, and quality of life, respectively.

Results: Hand tremor (75%) was the most common presenting feature, followed by ataxia (15%). Mean MOCA score was 22.87 ± 4.86, with 32 patients (53.34%) having mild cognitive dysfunction. Mean HAM-A score was 8.58 ± 4.09, with 40 patients (66.67%) having mild anxiety. Mean HAM-D score was 9.45 ± 4.48, with 39 patients (65%) having mild depression. Sleep abnormalities were seen in 21 patients (35%).

Conclusions: The burden of non-ataxia manifestations was observed to be high in our study. Hand tremor was the most common and initial non-ataxia manifestation of SCA12, which may be misdiagnosed as essential tremor or parkinsonian tremor. Cognitive and sleep abnormalities and quality of life parameters correlated with severity of ataxia. Recognition and assessment of non-ataxia manifestations may help in providing holistic care to patients with SCA12.

Deepshikha Singla, Bhupender Kumar Bajaj

Vardhman Mahavir Medical College, New Delhi (VMMC, New Delhi), India

Background and Aim: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is a neurologic disorder characterized by raised intracranial pressure of unknown etiology. Cognitive dysfunction has been reported in patients with IIH, and this can have negative impact on the quality of life of patients with IIH. The relationship between IIH and cognitive impairment is not well studied. We undertook this study with the aim to assess neurocognitive and neuropsychiatric dysfunction in patients with IIH and to determine their relationship with the clinical features of IIH and lumbar cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) opening pressure.

Methodology: This was a case–control cross-sectional observational study in which 34 patients and 34 age- and gender-matched healthy controls were recruited. Detailed clinical evaluation including comprehensive neurocognitive assessment was done using Indian Council of Medical Research-Neurocognitive Toolbox (ICMR-NCTB) for patients and controls. Neuropsychiatric Inventory Questionnaire was used to screen for neuropsychiatric comorbidities. Headache severity was measured using Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6), and lumbar puncture was done for all the patients.

Results: The mean age (± standard deviation [SD]) of patients and controls were 34.38 (±8.623) and 33.29 (±7.783) years, respectively. Mean (±SD) of HIT-6 score and lumbar CSF pressure were 63.26 (±11.944) and 291.91 (±31.09) mm CSF, respectively. Patients performed significantly worse compared to controls on assessment of cognitive function by ICMR-NCTB with Montreal Cognitive Assessment, Trail Making Black and White A and B tests, phonemic fluency, verbal delayed recall, picture naming test, and Modified Taylor Complex Figure test (P < 0.05). Anxiety, depression, and appetite dysfunction were significantly higher in patients compared to controls (P < 0.05).

Conclusions: Patients with IIH have multidomain cognitive impairment, which correlates with lumbar CSF pressure.

Mahammad Mondal, Faheem Arshad, Keerthana BS, Pallavi Nagaraj Sastry, Suvarna Alladi

National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro-Sciences, Bengaluru (NIMHANS, Bengaluru), Karnataka, India

Background and Aim: Dementia is a major public health challenge due to limited therapies for degenerative forms; yet a notable portion of cases are potentially reversible, emphasizing the importance of actively identifying and promptly treating reversible causes. Our study aims to investigate the prevalence, etiologic spectrum, and clinical indicators predicting reversible dementia.

Methodology: This retrospective study was conducted at a South Asian neuroscience institute from 2017 to 2023 and included patients with cognitive decline and potentially reversible etiologies. Thorough investigations and red flag assessments were conducted.

Results: Out of 1810 dementia cases, 370 (20.4%) had reversible dementia (ReDem). ReDem patients were younger (56.2 vs. 61.9 years) with shorter illness duration (20.9 vs. 24.0 months) than degenerative dementia (DD) patients (P < 0.001). Reversible etiologies included immune-mediated conditions (20.0%), neuroinfectious diseases (6.6%), psychiatric causes (7.6%), nutritional and metabolic etiologies (10.5%), neurosurgical conditions (14.6%), and miscellaneous etiologies (12.2%). All studied red flags, except seizures, were more common in ReDem patients compared to DD patients (P < 0.05). Binary logistic regression showed red flags increasing odds of reversible causes, such as early onset (odds ratio [OR]: 2.35), fluctuations (OR: 3.73), rapid decline (OR: 3.02), high-risk exposure (OR: 11.76), high-risk behavior (OR: 35.88), incongruent neuropsychologic assessment (OR: 35.15), abnormal general physical examination (OR: 8.79), and unexplained neurologic findings (OR: 13.82). The presence of >1 red flag increased odd by 5.94 times, >2 by 20.69 times, and >3 by 25.14 times (P < 0.05 for all). Treatment was provided to all ReDem patients, but 64.1% were lost to follow-up, with the mortality reported being 5.1%. Of the 35.9% followed, 63.9% reported subjective improvement and 31.6% showed Clinical Dementia Rating improvement (mean CDR: 1.3).

Conclusions: This study, the largest on this topic in India and one of the largest globally, emphasizes the importance of recognizing and treating reversible causes of dementia, including comorbidities in DD cases.

Government medical college, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India

Background and Aim: Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) is a serious complication of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS). The study was undertaken to determine the predictors and outcome of sICH.

Methodology: In this prospective cohort study conducted at ****, between May 2023 and May 2024, adult patients with AIS undergoing IVT were recruited. sICH was defined as per the European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study (ECASSIII) criteria, and the cohort was followed up and various clinicoradiologic parameters and outcome were compared between groups with and without sICH to determine the risk factors using a logistic regression analysis and prognosis, respectively. Predictive efficacy of risk prediction models – HAT, SEDAN, THRIVE, SPAN100 – were compared.

Results: Out of the 120 patients thrombolysed, sICH occurred among 9.17%, and all of them had a parenchymal bleed of PH2 category (with extra-axial bleed in two cases). The performance of predictive scores HAT ≥ 3, SEDAN > 3, THRIVE > 5, and SPAN100 = 1 was only modest. Seven of the 11 patients with sICH succumbed to death within a 3-month span.

Conclusions: The study identified five independent risk factors for sICH after multivariate logistic regression – the highest odds was for stroke severity followed by presence of large vessel occlusion, hyperdense middle cerebral artery sign on initial computed tomography, exposure to dual antiplatelet and total anterior circulation stroke. Among the risk prediction scores studied, HAT had the best discriminatory capacity.

Yerasu Muralidhar Reddy, Lalitha Pidaparthi, Jagarlapudi MK Murthy, Kiran ESS, Sudeer Kumar

Renova Institute of Neurological Sciences (RINS), Hyderabad, Telangana, India

Background and Aim: Hansen’s ulnar neuropathy (HUN) and entrapment ulnar neuropathy, commonly referred to as ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (UNE), are the most common causes of focal ulnar neuropathies. Differentiating the two is sometimes challenging. We aimed to examine the utility of the ultrasound (US) in differentiating these conditions.

Methodology: We performed a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from 26 nerves of 22 HUN patients and 36 nerves of 28 UNE patients who underwent US. The ulnar nerve cross-sectional area (CSA) was measured at the elbow behind the medial epicondyle, 5 cm proximal and distal to the elbow. The length of the enlarged nerve and the humerocubital nerve ratio (HCR) were calculated. All these parameters were compared between UNE and HUN.

Results: CSA of the ulnar nerve was significantly higher in HUN at all three measurement sites than in UNE (P < 0.001). The maximum CSA was noted above the elbow in HUN and at the elbow in UNE (P < 0.001). Lengthy enlarged segment was characteristic of HUN (P < 0.001). HCR was also significantly different between the two groups (P < 0.001). The optimum cut-off of HCR (for HUN) was 0.87 (sensitivity 88%, specificity 100%, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.95).

Conclusions: HCR is a useful sonographic indicator for distinguishing HUN and UNE. Other variable favoring HUN is extensive and maximal nerve enlargement above the elbow. UNE is characterized by focal nerve enlargement at the elbow.

Sohini Chakraborty, Awadh Kishor Pandit, M. V. Padma Padma Srivastava, Rohit Bhatia, Manjari Tripathi, Deepti Vibha, Vishnu V. Y., Rajesh Singh, Achal Kumar Srivastava, Ajay Garg, B. D. Charan, Ashish Upadhyaya

All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi (AIIMS, New Delhi), India

Background and Aim: Stroke is the fourth leading cause of death and fifth leading cause of disability in India. Our aim was to assess predictors of good functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0–2) at 3 months and early neurologic improvement [ENI] = National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) reduction by 8 or NIHSS of 0/1 at 24 h) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients.

Methodology: A single-center prospective cohort study recruiting 311 adult AIS patients with pre-stroke mRS?1, within 72 h of ictus, fulfilling the inclusion and exclusion criteria, was conducted from February 2022 till November 2023. Demographic data, onset to hospital arrival (Time1), Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) motor score at presentation, NIHSS at presentation (NIHSS0), at 24 h (NIHSS24), and at 72 h (NIHSS72), systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score (CT-ASPECTS), multiphase-computed tomography angiogram collateral score, perfusion study (Computed Tomography Perfusion), time to intravenous thrombolysis (IVT)/thrombectomy (EVT), single/dual antiplatelet, electrocardiogram, echocardiography, Holter, hemogram, electrolytes, coagulogram, lipid, thyroid, ENI and mRS at 3 months (mRS3) were assessed.

Results: Of the study subjects, 66% were males, having a mean age of 56 years (±16.18). 53% were hypertensive, 35% were diabetic, 33% had dyslipidemia, 38% consumed tobacco while 23% consumed alcohol. In addition, 22%, 31%, 27%, 5%, and 14% had small vessel disease (SVD), large artery atherosclerosis, cardioembolic stroke, stroke of other determined etiology, and stroke of other undetermined etiology, respectively. Mean SBP, DBP, GCS, NIHSS at presentation, CT-ASPECTS, collateral score, time to hospital arrival, time to thrombolysis, and time to thrombectomy were 147 mmHg (±28.58), 86 mmHg (±16.4), 6 (±1), 11 (6–17), 6 (±3), 3 (±1), 6.5 h (3.5–12.5), 5.5 h (3.5–9), and 3.5 h (2.5–4.5), respectively. Moreover, 52% had LVO and 38% achieved ENI. On univariate analysis, younger age of ictus, lower NIHSS at 0, 24, and 72 h, higher GCS at presentation, higher CT-ASPECTS, absence of LVO, higher mTCA collateral score, TOAST of SVD, ENI, absence of cardiac chamber enlargement on echocardiography, absence of arrhythmia diagnosed by either echocardiogram/electrocardiogram/Holter, intake of dual antiplatelet, those who did not undergo decompression surgery, higher serum albumin, lower C-reactive protein, lower D-dimer, lesser time from ictus to hospital, and reduced duration of hospital stay, all were prognostic factors for good outcome at 3 months. On performing multivariate regression, NIHSS at presentation, age, achieving ENI, intake of DAPT, and absence of arrythmia were independent predictors of good outcome at 3 months after adjusting for confounders. With increase in age and NIHSS at 0 h, chances of good outcome significantly decreased with adjusted odds ratio of 0.943 (0.889–0.999, P = 0.049) and 0.791 (0.656–0.954, P = 0.014), respectively, whereas ENI, usage of DAPT, and absence of arrythmia had higher odds of achieving good outcome with odds ratio (OR) of 68.688 (28.127–167.742), 0.268 (0.096–0.749), and 0.296 (0.091–0.962), respectively. On performing multivariate regression, lower admission NIHSS, IVT, use of DAPT, absence of arrythmia, and right hemispheric stroke were significant predictors of ENI after adjusting for confounding factors. With the increase in NIHSS at 0 h, chances of ENI significantly decreased with adjusted odds ratio of 0.795 (0.717–0.881, P < 0.0001). With IVT, use of DAPT, absence of arrythmia, and right hemispheric stroke, odds of ENI increased with OR of 4.312 (2.258–8.233), 0.077 (0.015–0.395), 0.226 (0.112–0.456), and 0.153 (0.058–0.406), respectively.

Conclusions: Prediction of outcome after AIS is important for setting realistic and attainable treatment goals. It informs patients and their relatives properly, facilitates discharge planning, and helps in anticipating possible consequences. Improving our knowledge about predictive factors might enhance rehabilitative procedures in AIS patients.

Background and Aim: Cognitive impairments in idiopathic Parkinson’s disease (IPD) patients is an important nonmotor symptom that is ignored most of the time. Background and Aim: Perforating artery infarction (PAI) with branch atheromatous disease has a stroke recurrence risk of 18%–33%, and there is also high risk of early neurologic deterioration. Topiwala National Medical College and BYL Nair Charitable Hospital, Mumbai (TNMC, Mumbai), Maharashtra, India

Background and Aim: Brivaracetam (BRV), a third-generation antiseizure medication (ASM), offers strong conformational receptor domain binding, faster blood-brain barrier permeability, and better tolerability, making it a potential therapeutic option as an initial line or initial line add-on strategy for focal-onset seizure (FoS). The following study was planned to further understand the role and relevance of BRV in the real-world settings of India.

Methodology: This was a multicentric, cross-sectional, noninterventional study conducted in patients with FoS across India. The study was approved by the central independent ethics committee. Descriptive and analytical statistics were employed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences version 29.0.1.0.

Results: Per protocol analysis included 8479 eligible patients from 1069 sites. Gender distribution showed 5771 (68.06%) were males and 2708 (31.93%) were females, with a mean age of 41.21 years (12.74 ± standard deviation). Totally, 8019 (94.57%) patients had FoS and 460 (5.43%) patients had focal to bilateral tonic–clonic seizures (FBTCs), with psychiatric comorbidities noted in 3884 (45.80%) cases. In FoS, BRV 50–100 mg twice a day (BID) was administered as monotherapy and as an adjuvant in 51.6% and 48.3% patients, respectively. In FBTCs, BRV 100 mg BID was administered as monotherapy and as an adjuvant in 50.20% and 49.7% patients, respectively. Sodium channel blocker (SCB), Na Valproate, and lacosamide were the most commonly prescribed ASM along with BRV.

Conclusions: BRV remains a pragmatic option for the management of FoS for the treatment-naïve and/or BAE cases.

Background and Aim: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is a rare, debilitating autoimmune condition characterized by severe inflammation of the optic nerves and spinal cord, leading to blindness and paralysis. The global incidence of NMOSD varies, with higher prevalence observed in certain ethnic groups such as Asians and Africans. In the USA, the prevalence is estimated at 1–10 per 100,000 individuals. Methodology: In our tertiary care center, we conducted a retrospective study and analyzed the clinical and demographic characteristics of a cohort of 47 NMOSD patients.

Background and Aim: Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) is often associated with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders (NMOSDs) or myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG)-Ab–associated disease. We aimed to study the difference in the clinical and radiologic features, treatment response, and recurrence of seronegative LETM, when compared to antibody-positive patients.

Methodology: A retrospective observational study was carried out in the inpatient department of neurology in a tertiary care center from April 2022 to April 2024. Written informed consent of the patients and approval from the Institutional Ethics committee were taken.

Results: Forty-three patients with LETM (20 seronegative, 14 anti-AQP4 Ab, and nine anti-MOG positive) were included. Majority (91.3%) of the females had antibody-positive LETM, whereas 60% males had seronegative LETM. At the onset, both groups displayed similar average in modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores. However, on follow-up, both the groups exhibited significant reduction in mRS score. Eleven patients experienced at least one relapse (6 [26.1%] seropositive and 5 [25%] seronegative).

Conclusions: Patients with seronegative LETM have clinical and radiologic differences when compared to those with seropositive LETM. However, the response to early immunotherapy is beneficial and prevents relapses and disability.

Background and Aim: Pure neuritic leprosy (PNL) is an uncommon form of leprosy involving peripheral nerves alone. Background and Aim: New daily persistent headache (NDPH) is a continuous, unremitting headache from onset that yields suboptimal results with traditional medications. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has emerged as a promising noninvasive treatment for migraine. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy of rTMS in reducing the frequency and severity of headaches and associated anxiety and depressive symptoms in NDPH patients.

Methodology: This was an open-label, prospective, single-arm, interventional pilot study conducted between October 2022 and September 2023. All eligible participants received 10 Hz rTMS (600 pulses, 10 trains), delivered to the left prefrontal cortex. The post-rTMS headache severity was recorded weekly for 4 weeks and headache-free days/functional disability, Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), and Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7 item (GAD-7) scores were recorded at the end of 4 weeks and compared with pre-rTMS parameters. The primary outcome was defined by 50% reduction in headache severity/headache-free days and 6 points reduction in Headache Impact Test-6 score at 4 weeks.

Results: Fifty NDPH patients (mean [standard deviation {SD}] age, 35.06 [13.91] years; 31 females [62%]) participated in this study. Thirty-five patients (70%) reported 50% improvement in pain severity, with a mean reduction of 10.84 (4.88) headache days. Thirty-eight patients (76%) reported a 6 points reduction in HIT score at 4 weeks. Maximum improvement in the above parameters was observed in NDPH patients with chronic migraine. Only two patients reported sound intolerance. The median (interquartile range) PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores reduced from 11.5 (3.75–20) to 7 (2–15) (P < 0.001) and from 10 (3–14) to 5.5 (0–9) (P < 0.001), respectively.

Conclusions: rTMS was well tolerated and effective in reducing pain severity, headache days and headache-related disability, and depressive and anxiety symptoms.

Background and Aim: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)/motor neuron disorder is a life-limiting, relentlessly progressive neurodegenerative condition.
